amy: quick follow-up to the kernel-selection RFC — thinking about a lightweight SM feature probe at startup to pick A100/H100/L4 codepaths. TL;DR: runtime probe + per-model profile, prefer explicit capability gating over heuristics. thoughts?

ben: love the idea. main worry is perf cliff if probe picks a path that falls back at runtime (eg missing fp8/te). how do we detect and recover quickly? :thinking_face: @amy

charlie: +1 for explicit capability mask and a kernel registry. runtime flow idea: 1) probe SM feature bits 2) compute capability_mask 3) pick registered kernel variant or fallback. pseudo: ```
cap = probe_sm();
variant = kernel_registry.lookup(model, cap);
if (!variant) variant = kernel_registry.lookup(model, GENERIC);
launch(variant);
```

raj: note: H100 has transformer-engine-style fast paths (fp8/te) that change numerical behavior. we need a policy: prefer those when available, but allow "force-generic" env var for validation. also add a safety-check after first batch to verify outputs within epsilon, then keep or rollback.

natalie: probing overhead matters for cold starts. we should cache probe result per-host and persist in node metadata. also do a quick micro-benchmarked warmup for the selected kernel to verify throughput/loss before routing traffic.

amy: good point on warmup. idea: probe fast (register-level flags), then do a single small warmup run measuring latency and a quick checksum diff against a reference implementation (FP16/generic) if available. if mismatch > threshold, mark variant as incompatible and fallback.

deploy-bot: CI: kernel-selection smokebench #842 succeeded on A100-emulation (latency ok) :white_check_mark:

ben: tradeoffs: more kernel variants -> bigger test matrix and build artefacts. proposal: two-tier variants: OPTIMIZED (architecture-specific) + GENERIC (portable). only publish OPTIMIZED after passing canary on 2 nodes.

charlie: agree. also want clear runtime API for kernel authors: metadata block with required SM features, numeric-mode (fp16/fp8/tf32), and validation hooks. example metadata block: ```
{
  "name":"attention_fastpath_v2",
  "requires":["mma.async_copy","tensor_core_fp8","warp_shuffle_mask"],
  "numeric":"fp8",
  "validation_cmd":"./validate_attention.sh"
}
```

raj: plus add capability for graceful degradation: fallback_policy could be `fallback_to_generic` or `reject_request` or `approximate_degrade`. customers can pick per-route.

amy: sounds like consensus. puts the onus on kernel package authors to include metadata + validation. infra tasks: probe caching, warmup harness, per-host capability store, expose env var to force path. product task: expose fallback_policy in model config.

natalie: I'll sketch a perf budget for warmup (should be < 200ms per model) and add it to infra runbook.

ben: test matrix note — we should run numeric-regression evals (existing eval harness) automatically on canaries for each OPTIMIZED variant.

amy: action items: @charlie write kernel metadata schema PR, @natalie add warmup budget + node cache design, @raj add validation script pattern + rollback hook, infra to add env var `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL` and node store. i'll coordinate RFC update.

charlie: I'll open PR with schema + lookup API by EOD.

deploy-bot: benchmark-run #843 queued on h100-canary

amy: thanks all — let's keep this lightweight and iterative. we'll land basic probe + generic fallback first, then add OPTIMIZED canaries. :rocket:
